summary: Harold Walter Bailey worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Western Australia and the University of Oxford under Frederick William Thomas. He held posts at SOAS and the University of Cambridge (1936–1967).

Haroon Khan Sherwani was a historian and Indologist who studied at Aligarh Muslim University and the University of Oxford, later mentored by Ghulam Yazdani. His posts included Osmania University (~1919–1946), Nizam College (~1946–1948), and Zakir Husain Delhi College (~1948–1951).
Harry Falk is an Indologist. He held posts at the University of Freiburg (~1978–1990) and served as Director at the Free University of Berlin (1993–2012).

Hartmut Buescher works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Chandrabhāl Tripāṭhī and held positions at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library (attested 2007).
Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his doctorate under Paul Thieme and held an academic post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel is an Indologist. His appointments include positions at the Katalogisierung der Orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (attested 1989), the Berlin State Library (attested 1992–1994), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2008).
Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Gakushuin University and the University of Tokyo. He held a professorship at Nagasaki University (~1978–2003).
Haruka Yanagisawa was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He held academic posts at Chiba University (~1980–1994) and the University of Tokyo (~1994–2007).

Harumi Hirano Ziegler specializes in Buddhist studies. She completed both her MA and PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Harunaga Isaacson specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Groningen and Leiden under Hans T. Bakker, Tilmann Vetter, and Albrecht Wezler. He held posts at Oxford, the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of Hamburg.

Harushige Takatsu was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and at the University of Oxford. His career included posts at the University of Tokyo and Musashi University (from 1968).

Harvey B. Aronson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed doctoral studies under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and co-director at Dawn Mountain (attested 2001).

Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia was an Indian archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at University College London (~1934–1936) and served as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1939–1973).

Haya Akegarasu was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and Shimei Futabatei at Otani University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. He later served as head of administration at Higashi Hongan-ji (~1951–1954).

Hayao Kawai was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1952). He held posts at Tenri University (~1959–1969), Kyoto University (~1992–2007), and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1995–2001).
Heather Stoddard specializes in Tibetology, sinology, and history and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London and under D. C. Lau, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas.

Heeraman Tiwari is an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the universities of Lucknow, Delhi, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He held posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Heidelberg University (2011–2012), and the Israel Institute for Advanced Studies.

Hegoda Khemananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. His career includes serving as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena (attested 1993) and Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya (attested 1993).

Heidi Fjeld is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Oxford and the University of Oslo under doctoral supervisor Signe Howell. She later worked as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Oslo (~2007–2011).

Heidi I. Koppl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Copenhagen under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer, and also studied under Khenpo Sherab Zangpo.
